questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was foreign and completely new for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
You got plenty of help from the school, and they were very accessible on mail even before the stay started. 

I lived in the dormitory on campus, and they were extremely helpful, both with requests regarding the dormitory, but also other issues you could need help with in Japan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You were guided into your dormitory and got a tour of both the campus and the dorm, to show the many different facilities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could choose to live at the Dormitory in tama or in seiseki. I lived in Tama, and it was really satisfied with my choice!

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen that was accessible at all times.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to get a lot of international friends! :) The room itself is sufficient for your needs, its about 8-9 square meters with a bed, aircondition etc. The kitchen is very large, and I have personally never experienced that there wasn't enough space for me to cook.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You were asked to fill out a couple questionnaires to choose how you wanted to live, seiseki (closer to centrum in Tokyo) Tama (in the Tama campus) or if you wanted to figure it out yourself. It was not difficult, but make sure to adhere to the deadlines! :)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could again write to the front office for the dormitory, and they were again very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit overwhelming in the beginning, but make sure to follow the different deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a mixed bag, some courses were very academic, and some were not.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar in some courses, very different in others.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I chose a japanese language course, IT Strategy, Business Communication, Business Negotiation, Philosophy, Global Tutorial, International Product Development and Cognitive Marketing.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend Cognitive Marketing and International Product Development, and if you want to learn japanese, the japanese language course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Put some money to the side to experience stuff. You're in Japan!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation prices can very quickly run up if you go to Tokyo centrum a lot. Food is however very cheap if you choose to eat in the cafeteria, or cook yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I played volleyball, which was very fun! :) They didn't talk a lot of english, but you can still communicate a little bit in English.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join a lot of different "circles". A list of these can be seen on Chuo's website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Play some sport or participate in the foreign exchange forum on campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to the outskirts of Tokyo or do some day trips. AND most importantly, eat some good japanese food! Good sushi, unagi, kaiseki etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: You adjust pretty quickly. People will not get mad at you if you don't adhere to the public norms, especially in public transportation, the japanese are too polite for that, but expect some weird looks if you don't.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I used the facilities in the dormitory a lot to meet the local students, and I made a lot of Japanese friends this way.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say that there was any particularly challenging aspects of Japanese culture. Danish culture is also very polite. Maybe the fact that you don't disturb people in the train, keep quiet or don't talk too loud.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the polite nature of all Japanese interactions. And of course the vibes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to meet more people! Your stay will be a lot more enjoyable if you do. 
Be ready to experience new stuff. 
Enjoy your stay, it's amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to quickly do your pre-approval of courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to interact with so many new foreign cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding enough energy to experience stuff all the time! Make sure to give yourself breaks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
